Recommendations relating to treatment of HIV (i.e. ART regimens) are frequently reviewed and revised and current guidelines (June 2013) are referred to in this guid- ance. The Panel recognized that ART improves treatment outcomes for TB in HIV-positive children. Management of drug-resistant TB in children (Chapter 7) Source of recommendation Rapid advice: treatment of tuberculosis in children. Geneva, World Health Organization, 2010 (WHO/HTM/TB/2010.13) n Recommendation 27 Children with proven or suspected pulmonary TB or tuberculous meningi- tis caused by multiple drug-resistant bacilli can be treated with a fluoro- quinolone in the context of a well-functioning MDR-TB control programme and within an appropriate MDR-TB regimen. The decision to treat should be taken by a clinician experienced in managing paediatric TB (Strong recommendation, very low quality evidence) Summary of recent evidence Many current recommendations that relate to the general management of drug-resistant TB are to be found in: Guidelines for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis - 2011 update. Geneva, World Health Organization, 2011 (WHO/HTM/ TB/2011.6). Other considerations The Panel recognized that these general recommendations were derived from very low quality of evidence; moreover, the evidence was from adults with drug-resistant TB. It also recognized that there are no standardized guidelines for the management of drug- resistant TB in children or for the management of child contacts of drug-resistant TB cases.
